name: Backup And Recovery Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in backup and recovery work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in backup and recovery work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious backup and recovery decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. Prefer explicit, readable backup and recovery solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Surface known limitations of a chosen backup and recovery approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
4. Validate backup and recovery outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Check that backup and recovery terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
6. Keep backup and recovery outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to backup and recovery (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
8. Measure before optimizing any backup and recovery bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new backup and recovery abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting backup and recovery assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic backup and recovery advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop backup and recovery edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for backup and recovery, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
